clue.text: Zero choice, quietly moving to find romantic elixir

parts.note: love is zero in a tennis score
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: moving says the quiet letter leaves its place in the word for choice and goes to the front

parts.note: an option is a choice
the quiet letter that moves

explanation.surface: With no options left, someone quietly sets off in search of a love philtre.
explanation.walkthrough: Love meaning nil is a tennis convention. The quiet letter is already in the word for choice; 'moving' only shifts it from second place to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A love potion is a magic drink said to make someone fall in love, the classic elixir of romance.

clue.text: Primarily, location inviting dipping outdoors?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the first letters of location, inviting, dipping and outdoors are L, I, D and O

explanation.surface: A description of a place that tempts people to take a swim in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: a lido is a spot that invites an outdoor dip.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool or bathing place.

clue.text: Meteorological device useless in broadcast

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard rather than read, so the answer sounds like the word

parts.note: vain means useless, as in a vain attempt

explanation.surface: A weather instrument proves useless during a forecast on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suits a weather forecast, but it signals a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather vane turns to show which way the wind is blowing.

clue.text: Before jobs advertised, terms often stated?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
posts that are advertised are positions, as in 'positions vacant'

explanation.surface: A note that job terms are often spelled out before the vacancies are advertised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' is itself one of the answer, which is why the definition is so loose: words like before, on and with are among the commonest stated.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepositions are short words such as on, in and before that are used constantly in speech and writing.

clue.text: Sweet time raising tiny creature with expensive coat

indicators.note: in a down answer raising means writing upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: an elf is a tiny mythical creature
a fur is an expensive coat

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale picture of a little creature in a fancy fur coat being brought up over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' works on both creature and coat together, since in a down answer they are written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A truffle is a rich chocolate sweet, named after the fungus it looks like.

clue.text: In Oxford English Dictionary, slang for 'hand' left out

indicators.note: the slang word goes in the dictionary's initials

parts.note: mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A complaint that a slang word for hand has been left out of the great dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' tells the slang word to go inside the dictionary's three initials, after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitted means excluded or not included.

clue.text: Without partisanship? Not entirely …

indicators.note: only part of the word partisanship is used, a run of its letters

parts.note: the answer sits in the middle of partisanship, after its first five letters

explanation.surface: A question about being free of party bias, trailing off.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in the middle of PARTISANSHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Sans is a borrowing from French meaning without, as in Shakespeare's 'sans teeth'.

clue.text: Fond of food, topless, enormous

indicators.note: in a down answer the top of a word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: gastronomic relates to good eating and fine food

explanation.surface: A greedy eater described as hungry and huge.
explanation.walkthrough: GASTRONOMIC loses its first letter, G.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomic, like astronomical, describes something vast, as large as the distances in space.

clue.text: Customer for whom every purchase is a steal?

definitions.text: Customer for whom every purchase is a steal?

parts.words: Customer for whom every purchase is a steal?
parts.note: a steal usually means a bargain, but here every 'purchase' is literally stolen from the shop

explanation.walkthrough: A bargain is called a steal; this so-called customer pays nothing at all because the goods are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoplifter takes goods from a shop without paying, posing as a customer.

clue.text: DJ's tunes displaying acumen: disco, mostly

indicators.note: displaying read as dis-playing, playing out of order, signals that the letters are rearranged
mostly means most of the word, so the last letter of disco goes

explanation.surface: A DJ shows off skill with a selection of disco records.
explanation.walkthrough: ACUMEN and DISC (disco, mostly) are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Dance music is the kind of music a DJ plays for people to dance to.

clue.text: Shakespearean ass stripped off, revealing German lad

indicators.note: stripped means having its outer layer removed, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: Bottom is the weaver turned into an ass in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A naked Shakespearean actor reveals himself to be a German boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ass' and 'stripped off' suggest a bare bottom, but Bottom is the character; losing its outer letters leaves OTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German boy's name.

clue.text: Another swindle from junior partner

parts.note: a second helping is another one
a fiddle is a swindle or fraud

explanation.surface: One more fraud carried out by a junior member of a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from 'playing second fiddle', taking the lesser role.
explanation.definitionFit: Second fiddle is a person in a subordinate role, like the second violinist in an orchestra.

clue.text: Paper in error, ultimately, with the glib Grease To Lose Steam

parts.note: a goof is a blunder or error
the FT, the Financial Times, is a British newspaper

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letters of the three words are taken

parts.note: the last letters of with, the and glib are H, E and B
oil is grease or lubricant

explanation.surface: A garbled headline about a newspaper's slick blunder involving the musical Grease.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make Grease look like the film musical, but it is plain oil. FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off the boil is an idiom for losing energy or enthusiasm, like water cooling.

clue.text: Uselessly intervened — vis-à-vis wheel?

definitions.note: the phrase 'reinvented the wheel' means wasted effort redoing something that already exists

indicators.note: uselessly suggests the letters are not working as they should, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who interfered to no purpose, as with the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the idiom of reinventing the wheel, which suits the idea of pointless intervention.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheel is the classic example of something that is pointlessly reinvented, the idiom for wasted effort.

clue.text: Inertia — flipping extremes in inertia — then assumes proud position

indicators.note: the word inertia runs from I to A, so flipping those end letters means an I becomes an A

parts.note: a standstill is a state of no movement, inertia

explanation.surface: A body at rest, after a twist, rises and stands up proudly.
explanation.walkthrough: The extremes of the word inertia are I and A; flipping them turns the I of STANDSTILL into A.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand tall is to keep an upright, confident posture, showing pride.

clue.text: Topless bloke — given plonk — to start weaving?

indicators.note: topless means without its top, the first letter

parts.note: a gent is a man, a bloke
plonk is British slang for cheap wine

explanation.surface: A shirtless man, handed cheap wine, begins to sway about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weaving' suggests a drunk lurching about, but it is the craft of twisting threads together.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist or wind things together, which is how weaving begins.

clue.text: Unload — and snooze

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to set down passengers or goods

explanation.walkthrough: The same two-word phrase covers delivering a load and nodding off.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off can mean to deliver someone or something, or to doze.

clue.text: Might one of these have an issue with kids …?

definitions.text: Might one of these have an issue with kids …?

parts.words: Might one of these have an issue with kids …?
parts.note: an issue is a problem or offspring, and kids are children or young goats, so both childminders and female goats fit

explanation.walkthrough: A childminder may have problems with children, while a female goat has kids as her issue, her offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Nannies are both childminders and female goats, whose young are kids.

clue.text: Game licence's not beginning to show discipline

indicators.note: a game leg is a lame one, so the letters are put out of shape
the word loses its beginning, its first letter

parts.note: the word licence with the s from the possessive

explanation.surface: A hunting licence that cannot begin to show any rules.
explanation.walkthrough: LICENCES without L is ICENCES, whose letters are rearranged; 'Game' looks like hunting but means lame.
explanation.definitionFit: A science is a branch of study, an academic discipline.

clue.text: … Labour leader?

parts.note: Labour reads as the British political party, but it is childbirth, and this person leads a woman through it

explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes it the British Labour Party, but a labour here is a birth; the ellipsis carries on from the previous clue's kids.
explanation.definitionFit: A midwife guides and assists a mother through labour and childbirth.

clue.text: Taking some paracetamol, do VapoRub somewhere in E Europe

indicators.note: only some of the letters of paracetamol do VapoRub are taken, a run inside them

parts.note: the end of paracetamol, all of do and the start of VapoRub run together to spell the answer

explanation.surface: Medical advice: swallow a few pills and rub on some ointment while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'paracetamol' through 'do' into 'VapoRub'. VapoRub is a menthol chest rub.
explanation.definitionFit: Moldova is a country in eastern Europe between Romania and Ukraine.

clue.text: Aromatherapist's regular purchase, must-have painting

parts.note: essential means indispensable, a must-have
an oil is a painting done in oils

explanation.surface: An art collector's essential acquisition, an oil painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must-have painting' reads as one phrase about art, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential oils are concentrated plant extracts used in aromatherapy massage and burners.

clue.text: 'Terrible bore' largely describing Everyman as a writer

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing around, so the rearranged letters go around the I
terrible suggests something gone badly wrong, so the letters are rearranged
largely means most of the word, so the last letter of bore goes

parts.note: the setter is Everyman, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter is mocked as a dreadful bore of a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: BOR, bore largely, is rearranged as BRO, then wraps around I, the setter Everyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A biro is a ballpoint pen, an implement for writing with.

clue.text: No more than a lake

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a lake or pond, a poetic or dialect word

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is an adjective for smallness, the other an old noun for a body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, and a mere is also a lake, as in Windermere.

clue.text: Ruse; persona backfired

indicators.note: backfired read as fired back suggests the word is sent backwards

parts.note: a part is a role or persona played

explanation.surface: A trick involving an assumed identity goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: PART read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a trick or ruse to catch someone out.

clue.text: Gnome, idiot, ridiculously early

indicators.note: ridiculously means absurdly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A garden gnome and an idiot turn up absurdly early.
explanation.walkthrough: GNOME and IDIOT are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: In good time means with time to spare, early enough.

clue.text: Artist, Dutch heavyweight

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the world heavyweight boxing champion

explanation.surface: A painter described as a big name of Dutch art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch heavyweight' suggests a Dutch master like Rembrandt, but the artist is Spanish and the heavyweight a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dali was the Spanish surrealist painter.

clue.text: Becoming tongue-twisted, lay eyes on a foe, tentacled beast

indicators.note: said with a twisted tongue, the phrase slurs into something that sounds like the answer

parts.note: to lay eyes on a foe is to see an enemy

explanation.surface: Someone stammers on catching sight of an adversary, a tentacled monster.
explanation.walkthrough: Say SEE AN ENEMY quickly, as a tongue-twister, and it comes out close to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea anemone is a marine animal with a ring of stinging tentacles around its mouth.
